requirements.requirement: usb-storage kernel module stopped from loading now (immediate)
requirements.summary: Baseline showed usb_storage loaded (cmd-9aaed10a179d4620). Executor wrote /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf with blacklist + install /bin/false, unloaded via rmmod, and confirmed lsmod no longer shows it and explicit modprobe attempts are refused with 'Invalid argument' (cmd-3a0b162eead84e6a, cmd-b83799e901324a4d). Re-confirmed after the fix at cmd-9183967ff6274f32 and cmd-23782cd5a3cb4bc0.

requirements.requirement: usb-storage kernel module stopped from loading after reboot (persistent)
requirements.summary: First reboot (boot_id ca7b1f7b→c607b65d, cmd-ca8e7cfe87ba465b..cmd-8667496e33684891) directly demonstrated the initial fix was insufficient: post-reboot lsmod showed usb_storage reloaded (cmd-ffdf68725b7f45f5), and root cause was diagnosed as the extlinux kernel cmdline modules= parameter force-loading it pre-root-mount, bypassing modprobe.d (cmd-ce70a7583a484a0c). Executor removed usb-storage from /etc/update-extlinux.conf and regenerated /boot/extlinux.conf (cmd-c6a56044471c4733, cmd-226048be388c428d). A second reboot (boot_id c607b65d→a4b1bad6, cmd-15cd3c46db244493..cmd-0f6672bf73894770) confirmed the fix: post-reboot kernel cmdline no longer includes usb-storage, lsmod shows it absent, and explicit modprobe is refused (cmd-9183967ff6274f32). The a4b1bad6 boot_id matches the fixed after_executor snapshot, cross-confirming this was the final observed state.

requirements.requirement: Node health preserved / core services intact after change and reboot
requirements.summary: Post-fix rc-status shows networking, sshd, chronyd, vsock-agent, fsck, localmount all started (cmd-23782cd5a3cb4bc0). Package-health and listening-sockets snapshots show expected sshd/dhcpcd services running after executor changes with no failed-service indication (failed-services check unsupported on this Alpine image, not indicative of failure).

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — blocking usb-storage from loading immediately and across reboot — are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The executor's first reboot legitimately exposed that the modprobe blacklist alone was insufficient because Alpine's extlinux kernel cmdline force-loaded usb-storage pre-root-mount; it then fixed the root cause and proved persistence with a second reboot showing boot_id change and the module absent from both lsmod and the kernel cmdline. Core services remained healthy throughout.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare stage disabled for this task), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before/after-executor comparison, which is available and consistent.
Two small log files (/tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/reboot2.log) were left on the node; low-risk but technically unreverted residue from the restart trigger commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were all either read-only discovery, the blacklist/install directive write, the necessary rmmod/modprobe verification, or the extlinux cmdline edit needed to close the persistence gap discovered during the first reboot test. Both reboots were required: the first was the standard verification restart that happened to reveal a real gap, the second confirmed the corrective fix, matching the fixed boot-identity cross-check (ca7b1f7b→c607b65d→a4b1bad6). No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were found. Minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log and /tmp/reboot2.log (created by the background reboot-trigger commands cmd-bcc11ae524c444a0 and cmd-433a52349a194a5c) were left on the node per the after_executor snapshot diff, a small, low-risk, non-security-relevant leftover.
